title: Tenant fairness throttling and latency shelving for hosted API 5xx/timeouts during escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During two customer escalations on 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09 we observed sustained tenant-driven tails of 5xx and timeout errors in the Hosted API. Root cause analysis points to a combination of aggressive client-side retries, connection pooling contention at the edge proxy, and KV cache compaction thrashing on GPUs which amplified latencies and caused intermittent 5xx responses. The result was tenant-visible error spikes and heavier-than-expected downstream load which worsened eviction and kernel scheduling behavior.

Goals: implement an engineering playbook that (1) immediately reduces customer-visible failures, (2) prevents retry-amplification and connection starvation, (3) provides per-tenant fairness controls (concurrency + shelf queue), and (4) codifies rollout + observability for future escalations.

Short-term mitigation (hotfixes already applied):
- Edge proxy: added tenant-scoped concurrent request limits (per-tenant token bucket) with a small shared reserve for burst smoothing. Deployed to canary region 1 (us-west1) 2026-03-10 04:12 UTC.
- SDK defaults: lowered client retry attempts from 5->2 for common generator endpoints and added exponentially increasing jitter to backoff to avoid synchronized retries. Dist-tagged as sdk-rollback-2026.
- Connection pool tuning: increased max connections per worker and enabled staggered keepalive drain to prevent pool starvation during tenant bursts.
- KV cache: enabled background compaction window and limited synchronous compaction frequency during high CPU/GPU utilization to avoid IO/work scheduling spikes.

Planned/medium-term changes (next 2 sprints):
- Tenant fairness throttling: implement lease-based shelving queue that returns an HTTP 202 with estimated retry-after when a tenant exceeds steady-state concurrency thresholds. This preserves priority order while shedding load gracefully instead of triggering retries.
- Adaptive retry quarantine: when a tenant triggers >X 5xx in Y seconds, mark client tokens as 'quarantined' for soft-backoff and reduce their retry budget across edge proxies.
- Circuit breakers: per-route, per-tenant CB with automatic half-open probing and SLO-aware thresholds.
- Observability: new per-tenant histograms for queue wait time, retry amplification ratio, and connection hold time. Add alerting composite: (p95 latency > SLA && retry amplification ratio > 1.5) -> pager.
- Release & rollout: gated canary release across regions, start with non-production tenants and low-impact customers, then progressively widen to paid tenants.

Artifacts and links:
- Hotfix PR (edge proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3125
- SDK rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/879
- KV compaction tuning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1140
- Dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted/tenant-fairness-canary
- Initial customer comms draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abc-example

Acceptance criteria:
- Canaries show p95 latency improvement >= 30% under simulated tenant burst workload and 50% reduction in 5xx rate for impacted tenants.
- No regression in overall throughput for non-impacted tenants.
- New alerts fire with actionable context and link back to tenant-id and suggested remediation steps.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Shelving queue increases client-side complexity (clients must handle 202 + Retry-After) — mitigated by SDK changes that transparently handle shelf responses where possible.
- Aggressive quarantining can reduce availability for noisy customers; thresholds must be conservative with monitoring and manual override.
- Changes to KV compaction frequency may temporarily increase memory pressure; we will monitor compaction lag metrics and revert if regressions appear.

Follow-ups (post-release):
- Postmortem to include timeline, telemetry, and customer impact spreadsheet.
- Work with Solutions Engineering to prepare migration guidance for customers with high concurrency patterns.
- Add e2e chaos tests simulating tenant retry storms to prevent regression.
